title: Ex-Tekken director Harada: wishes hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released (Eurogamer, via Inven Global)

sources.name: Eurogamer, 'Ex-Tekken director Harada wishes Xbox Series S wouldn't have been released', Connor Makar, 11 Nov 2026 14:09 local
Inven Global (English translation of the Korean panel, cited by Eurogamer, not opened)

first_report: Eurogamer 11 Nov 2026 about 14:09 (18:09 Dubai), citing Inven Global
footage: Steam trailer 'TEKKEN 8 - Launch Trailer' (app 1778820), official Bandai Namco, stand-in for Harada's series, credited on screen

angle.hook: The man behind Tekken said, with a senior Xbox official in the room, that he wishes the Xbox Series S had never been released
angle.why_now: reported today from the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea
angle.what_it_means_here: Series S is the cheaper Xbox console sold in the Gulf; developers say it adds work to every Xbox release
angle.payoff: another panellist said the console forces them to optimise their code cleanly; Harada says Series S players blame developers, not Microsoft

checked: gate 14:50Z: Eurogamer article read in full 14:50Z (no update note); Inven Global original not opened; no denial or Microsoft reply found in the digest; single outlet, labelled تقرير

claims.text: Harada said at the CGDC 2026 panel (moderated by Shuhei Yoshida) he wishes hardware like Xbox Series S wouldn't be released, with a senior Xbox official attending
Harada: low memory is an issue, hardest part is a device so similar to Series X with awkwardly lower performance
Harada: Series S users direct complaints at developers rather than Microsoft
Another panellist (CD Projekt Red's Pawel Sasko): the console constantly throws challenges and forces very clean optimisation
